item.title: Compressions of Linear Relations in Krein Spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.07299v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Given an orthogonal decomposition \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}} = \mathfrak{H}[\dotplus]\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) of a Krein space, we study compressions \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)\) of linear relations \(R\) in \(\widetilde{\mathfrak{H}}\) to \(\mathfrak{H}\). We formulate a sufficient condition that ensures that compression commutes with taking adjoints, that is, the adjoint identity \({\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R^{\widetilde{*}}) = {\mathrm{C}_{\mathfrak H}}(R)^{*}\) holds. We derive preservation and reflection results for the compression of maximal dissipative, maximal symmetric, and self-adjoint linear relations. For nonnegative linear relations, the adjoint identity also implies that compression commutes with taking the Friedrichs extension. For \(\mathfrak{H}\ne\{0\}\), we characterize finite dimensionality of the exit space \(\widehat{\mathfrak{H}}\) by universal compression properties. Finally, we give a criterion for the adjoint identity to hold in terms of bounded linear functionals on \(R\).
item.dc:creator: Branko \'Curgus, Aad Dijksma

item.title: Holomorphic calculus on $L^p(\ell^q)$ I: optimal angles
item.description: arXiv:2611.07430v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $L$ generate a symmetric contraction semigroup. We prove a holomorphic H\"ormander calculus on $L^p(X;\ell^q)$ at the optimal angle $\max\{\arcsin|1-2/p|,\arcsin|1-2/q|\}$, with boundary Sobolev order $s>3$.
item.dc:creator: Dangyang He

item.title: Singular values of iterated Aluthge transforms of compact operators
item.description: arXiv:2611.07728v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Yamazaki proved that the norms of the iterated Aluthge transforms of an operator converge to its spectral radius, and Ando showed that for matrices the singular values of the iterates converge to the moduli of the eigenvalues. We prove that the latter holds for every compact operator on a Hilbert space and every generalized Aluthge transform $\Delta_t$ with $0<t<1$: for every $j$, the $j$-th singular value of the $n$-th iterate converges to $|\lambda_j(T)|$, and the products of the $k$ largest singular values, as well as the Ky Fan norms, decrease monotonically to their limits. This is the Aluthge counterpart of the Yamamoto--Davis theorem. We also determine the limit in the Schatten $p$-norm whenever $T$ belongs to a strictly smaller Schatten class.
item.dc:creator: Hranislav Stankovi\'c

item.title: The Approximation Property without the Bounded Approximation Property in a Separable Banach Space and Its Dual
item.description: arXiv:2611.07930v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We investigate whether a dual Banach space with the approximation property (AP) must necessarily have the bounded approximation property (BAP). Using a quantitative renorming theorem for the space of absolutely summable sequences, we establish a direct-sum construction yielding a negative answer. More precisely, we construct a separable Banach space (X) such that both (X) and its dual (X^*) have the approximation property, while neither space has the bounded approximation property. The construction uses a sequence of equivalent renormings of (\ell_1) with increasingly restrictive finite-dimensional approximation bounds. By assembling these spaces through a (c_0)-direct sum, we obtain a dual space whose approximation property is preserved, but whose approximation constants cannot be uniformly bounded. We establish the required transfer principles, including the preservation of approximation bounds under complemented coordinate projections and the descent of the bounded approximation property from a dual space to its predual. We also provide an explicit complex-scalar version of the construction. The argument separates the external quantitative renorming input from the direct-sum construction and its functional-analytic consequences. In particular, the resulting example demonstrates that the approximation property of a dual space does not imply its bounded approximation property, even when the predual is separable and both spaces possess the approximation property.
item.dc:creator: Ma Yicen

item.title: Recovering the Length of a Path from its Signature
item.description: arXiv:2611.08030v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove the length conjecture of J. Chang, T. Lyons and H. Ni for paths of bounded variation for arbitrary real Banach spaces and any reasonable tensor (algebra) norms. More precisely, we establish the missing lower bound and in this way show that the length of a tree-reduced path is recovered from the asymptotic behaviour of its normalised signature. The main technical argument uses the norm duality and shuffle algebra to express natural powers of polygonal length approximations as combinations of linear functionals acting on restricted signatures, which are then glued by suitable integrations into a linear functional of controlled growth acting on the full signature. In particular, the full proof combines tools of classical analysis and functional analysis, such as localisation by continuous cutoff functions, Stone-Weierstrass approximation of continuous functions by signature polynomials, the Hahn-Banach theorem and a support detection lemma for compactly supported real signed Borel measures.
item.dc:creator: Felix Medwed

item.title: Non-standard behaviour of semibounded forms and their representations
item.description: arXiv:2611.08225v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A number of results is presented concerning the extreme behaviour of products of linear operators or relations from one Hilbert space ${\mathfrak H}$ to another Hilbert space ${\mathfrak K}$. It is shown that there exists a relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ such that the closure of the nonnegative relation $T^*T$ in ${\mathfrak H}$ is not equal to the nonnegative selfadjoint relation $T^*T^{**}$; moreover, this may happen for a singular but also for a regular (i.e., closable) relation $T$. In fact, as an extreme situation the paper contains a construction of a densely defined closable operator $T$, such that ${\rm dom\,}T^*T=\{0\}$, while $T^*T^{**}$ is a densely defined selfadjoint operator. Likewise it is shown that there exist a linear relation $T$ from ${\mathfrak H}$ to ${\mathfrak K}$ and a nonnegative everywhere defined contraction $R$ in ${\mathfrak K}$ for which the product $RT$ is singular and the product $R^{1/2} T$ is regular. Such results illustrate situations that can arise in the Lebesgue type decomposition of linear relations and the Lebesgue type decomposition of semibounded forms.
item.dc:creator: Seppo Hassi, Henk de Snoo

item.title: A centroaffine perspective on improved Brascamp--Lieb and dimensional Brunn--Minkowski inequalities
item.description: arXiv:2611.08283v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study dimensional concavity properties of even log-concave measures within the framework of weighted centroaffine differential geometry. We express the relevant local concavity inequalities in terms of a weighted Hilbert--Brunn--Minkowski operator and establish an anisotropic Poincar\'e inequality for odd functions and a strengthened Brascamp--Lieb inequality for even functions. As applications, we obtain quantitative dimensional concavity estimates for a class of geometric measures and measures with pinched Hessian, extending results of Cordero-Erausquin and Rotem for rotationally invariant measures and Eskenazis and Moschidis for the Gaussian measure.
item.dc:creator: Sotiris Armeniakos, Alexander V. Kolesnikov, Jacopo Ulivelli

item.title: GNS-like representations of a quasi *-algebra in Krein spaces
item.description: arXiv:2611.08329v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this paper unbounded representations of quasi *-algebras on an indefinite inner product space are introduced and studied. After introducing the partial *-algebra of unbounded closable operators sharing a common dense domain in a Krein space, the appropriate notion of *-representation in this setting is developed, and a GNS-type construction for quasi *-algebras based on $\alpha$-positive sesquilinear forms is established. Furthermore, the notion of abstract conditional expectation is generalized to quasi *-algebras and how \emph{admissible} abstract conditional expectations $P$ give rise to representable $P$-forms is shown. The relation between $\alpha$-positive forms and $P$-forms is also clarified. Several examples are provided.
item.dc:creator: Giorgia Bellomonte

item.title: A half-line of Schur idempotent norms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08419v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Using a family of bipartite graphs constructed by hanging identical rooted trees at every vertex of a highly symmetric graph, we show that every sufficiently large real number is the norm of an idempotent Schur multiplier on the bounded operators on $\ell^2$. This answers a question previously raised by the author.
item.dc:creator: Rupert H. Levene

item.title: Gelfand numbers of Schatten class embeddings in the quasi-Banach range
item.description: arXiv:2611.08448v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove Conjecture 1.4 of Prochno and Strzelecki [J. Approx. Theory 277 (2022), 105736] on Gelfand numbers of embeddings between finite-dimensional Schatten classes. For $0<p\le1$ and indices bounded away from the ambient dimension by a fixed proportion, we obtain the conjectured lower bound, uniformly in the target exponent $2\le q\le\infty$. Together with the known upper estimate obtained by Hinrichs, Prochno and Vyb\'iral [Math. Ann., 380(3-4):1563-1593, 2021], this gives the exact asymptotic order in the previously unresolved range. As a consequence, we obtain a complete all-index description by combining our result with the estimates of Hinrichs, Prochno and Vyb\'iral and of Prochno and Strzelecki. The proof is deterministic and is based on Hilbert--Schmidt projections on rectangular matrix spaces.
item.dc:creator: Joscha Prochno

item.title: Noncommutative weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity over locally compact quantum groups
item.description: arXiv:2611.07168v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study weak almost periodicity and left uniform continuity for Hopf-von Neumann algebras and locally compact quantum groups. For a Hopf-von Neumann algebra $(M,\Gamma)$, we introduce the space ${\rm WAP}_{{\rm Bessel},\pi_u}(M_*)$ through norm convergence conditions on rows and columns of slices associated with Bessel families in the universal representation. We prove that this space is the largest $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm WAP}(M_*)$ when separately continuous lift of the co-multiplication is multiplicative, and that the two spaces coincide when $M$ is commutative. Furthermore, the algebra $\{x\in C_b(\mathbb{G}): \Gamma(x)\in M(C_0(\mathbb{G})\otimes C_b(\mathbb{G}))\}$ is characterized as the greatest left introverted $C^*$-subalgebra of ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ satisfying a left Bessel condition on $L^2(\mathbb{G})$. We also show that ${\rm LUC}(L^1(\mathbb{G}))$ is a $C^*$-algebra whenever the center of $C_0(\mathbb{G})$ contains an element on which the bounded counit is non-zero.
item.dc:creator: Ramin Faal, Amin Allah Khosravi, Hamid Reza Ebrahimi Vishki

item.title: Non-symmetric integral geometry: alternative reconstruction procedure with dual Radon transform
item.description: arXiv:2611.07376v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: In the note, we use the principles of non-symmetric integral geometry (non-integral geometry), related to the non-symmetric restricted integration measure, to extend the well-known relations traced from the Fourier slice theorem and the dual Radon transform. The proposed generalization is a very useful for the alternative restoration of the outset function. The latter impacts entirely on the image reconstruction process. The derived relations confirm the complexity of the inversion operator thanks for the symmetry breaking of integration measure.
item.dc:creator: I. V. Anikin

item.title: The dimension-free threshold for maximal sections of $\ell_p$
item.description: arXiv:2611.07619v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the existence of a sharp threshold $p_0 \approx 26.265\ldots$, such that for every $n\in\mathbb{N}$ and $p\geq p_0$, the volume maximizing section of the unit ball of $\ell_p^n$ is the section with Ball's hyperplane $(\frac{e_1+e_2}{\sqrt{2}})^\perp$, whereas for $p\in(2,p_0)$ the asymptotic maximizer as the ambient dimension $n\to\infty$ is the hyperplane orthogonal to the diagonal vector $\frac{e_1+\cdots+e_n}{\sqrt{n}}$.
item.dc:creator: Silouanos Brazitikos, Alexandros Eskenazis

item.title: Algebras, Kernels and Correspondences
item.description: arXiv:2611.07700v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: This is a nearly complete draft of our paper in which we attempt to do three things. First, we show that when formulated in the context of reproducing kernel correspondences over Rieffel's category, Normod-$M$, the Kolmogorov decomposition/representation theorem of Ball, Marx, and Vinnikov is functorial in $M$. Second, we investigate relations between our work and the work of Clou\^atre and Hartz concerning multipliers of reproducing kernels. This investigation leads to interesting questions about the geometry of the matricial unit disc associated with a correspondence over $M$. And third, we describe how some of the recent work of Salomon, Shalit and Shamovich may be formulated in our setting. This leads to the notion of subvarieties, their quotients, and their relation with the structure of reproducing correspondences.
item.dc:creator: Sibaprasad Barik, Paul S. Muhly, Baruch Solel

item.title: Geometric Functional Inequalities for Markov Processes: An Invitation via the Langevin Diffusion
item.description: arXiv:2611.07785v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Functional inequalities provide a language for reasoning about the long-time properties of ergodic Markov processes in terms of their macroscopic geometry. This article offers an informal introduction to functional inequalities for readers who are more familiar with probabilistic tools based around couplings, Lyapunov techniques, and similar. The main ideas are developed through the overdamped Langevin diffusion, where various functionals related to this convergence admit particularly transparent expressions, and for which the key associated inequalities -- namely, the Poincar\'{e} and logarithmic Sobolev inequalities -- are especially well-studied. We explain the qualitative content of these inequalities, what they imply about convergence to equilibrium, how they transform and compose under natural operations, and how they interface with classical probabilistic approaches. Related inequalities are discussed more briefly, and an annotated guide is provided for readers wishing to enter the wider literature.
item.dc:creator: Sam Power

item.title: Failure of P\'olya-Szeg\H{o} inequality for weighted nonlocal seminorm and on nonlocal C-K-N inequality
item.dc:creator: Prosenjit Roy, Vivek Sahu

item.title: An interpretation of the BMO boundedness of H\"ormander--Mikhlin multipliers
item.description: arXiv:2611.08192v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove a pointwise domination of Poisson variances for H\"ormander--Mikhlin multipliers on the real line. The estimate holds in operator order for operator-valued functions and gives a direct Fourier-side proof of BMO boundedness. The same argument gives an algebraic proof of the one-dimensional Schur multiplier estimate of Conde-Alonso, Gonz\'alez-P\'erez, Parcet and Tablate ( Annals of Mathematics, 2023), formulated here using Poisson BMO. The endpoint estimates are proved for $L^2$ functions and Hilbert--Schmidt operators; interpolation gives the corresponding $L^p$ and Schatten estimates.
item.dc:creator: Tao Mei

item.title: Fourier level inequalities on the discrete cube via complex hypercontractivity and Riesz transforms
item.description: arXiv:2611.08289v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Eldan's level-$1{:}3$ inequality is a central tool in his second-order correlation inequalities for increasing Boolean functions. His proof is going to Gaussian space and uses an entropy estimate for second Hermite tensors. We give a direct proof on the discrete hypercube. For increasing real-valued functions $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$, we prove $$ W_3[f,g]\ge -2W_1[f,g]\log\!\left(\frac{\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}}{W_1[f,g]}\right). $$ The proof combines complex hypercontractivity with the discrete Riesz transforms. We also give a short proof of a level-$1:d$ inequality obtained by Keller and Kindler. As an application, we recover Eldan's correlation inequality with a slight improvement. If $f,g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{0,1\}$ are increasing and $g$ is antipodal, then $$ \mathrm{Cov}(f,g)\ge \frac1{24}\,\frac{\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g]}{\sqrt{\log\!\left(4e\sqrt{\mathrm{Var}(f)\mathrm{Var}(g)}/(\sum_i\mathrm{Inf}_i[f]\mathrm{Inf}_i[g])\right)}}, $$ where the square-root logarithm cannot be improved as shown in the OR--majority example.
item.dc:creator: Fan Chang, Zhenyu Li, Guanghui Wang, Mingrui Wang

item.title: Characterization of Fr\'{e}chet Spaces and Application to Hausdorff MNC
item.description: arXiv:2005.01832v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the Hausdorff measure of noncompactness associated with compatible metrics on Fr\'echet spaces, with the aim of extending its Banach-space properties. After recalling the characterization by complete translation-invariant metrics with convex balls, we calculate the scalar Hausdorff measure for a standard weighted fractional metric. For bounded nonprecompact sets its value is the unique root of an equation involving a finite seminorm gauge determined by the covering radius. This yields an actual Hausdorff-condensing criterion for compact perturbations of maps having separate contraction constants at the seminorm levels. On countable products of Banach spaces we obtain an exact coordinate formula and a sharp scalar contraction bound on bounded domains, without requiring a uniform gap between the coordinate constants and one for strict condensation. For closed subspaces, an exact finite-projection formula retains the compatibility constraints on covering centers. Explicit examples show why separately computed seminorm measures cannot generally be substituted into the metric formula. Applications to spaces of real sequence-valued continuous functions give an explicit oscillation formula and exhibit the compatibility obstruction on an unbounded interval. Classical fixed-point consequences are recorded briefly.
item.dc:creator: Henning Wunderlich

item.title: Generalized gyrovector spaces revisited
item.description: arXiv:2403.15015v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We revise a proof of a Mazur-Ulam theorem for generalized gyrovector spaces.
item.dc:creator: Toshikazu Abe, Osamu Hatori

item.title: Sharp Finiteness Principles for the boundary values of $C^2$-functions
item.description: arXiv:2406.04431v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Let $\Omega$ be an arbitrary domain in ${\bf R}^n$, and let $C^2(\Omega)$ be the space of all functions whose partial derivatives of all orders up to two are continuous and bounded on $\Omega$. We prove the following Finiteness Principle for the boundary values of $C^2(\Omega)$-functions: A function $f$ defined on the boundary of $\Omega$ is the trace of a function $F\in C^2(\Omega)$ provided there exists $\lambda>0$ such that, for every set $E$ of at most $N=3\cdot 2^{n-1}$ boundary points, there exists a function $F_E\in C^2(\Omega)$ with $\|F_E\|_{C^2(\Omega)}\le\lambda$ whose trace coincides with $f$ on $E$. Moreover, $F$ can be chosen with $\|F\|_{C^2(\Omega)}\le\gamma\lambda$ where $\gamma$ depends only on $n$. We also refine this principle by showing that it suffices to consider $N$-point sets $E$ with specific geometric ``visibility'' properties relative to $\Omega$.
item.dc:creator: Pavel Shvartsman

item.title: A Hardy space approximation supporting zero-free half-planes for the $\zeta$-function
item.description: arXiv:2606.16097v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: An equivalent version of the B\'aez-Duarte criterion \cite{baez} for the Riemann Hypothesis (RH) by Bagchi states that the RH holds true if and only if the function $E(s) = 1/s$ belongs to the closed linear span of $G_k(s) = (k^{-s} - k^{-1})\zeta(s)/s,\, k \geq 2$ in the Hardy space \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_{1/2}) \), where $\mathbb{C}_{\alpha}$ denotes the half-plane $\mathrm{Re}(s)>\alpha$. We first show that if $E$ belongs to the closure of span$(G_k)_{k\geq 2}$ in \( H^2(\mathbb{C}_{\alpha}) \) for $\alpha>1/2$, then $\zeta$ is zero-free in $\mathbb{C}_\alpha$. We then use this as the basis for a numerical analysis of the sequence \[ s_n = \left\| \sum_{k=2}^{n} \mu(k) G_k - E \right\|^2_\alpha, \] for $1/2\leq \alpha \leq 1$, where $\left\|.\right\|_\alpha$ is the norm in $H^2(\mathbb{C}_{\alpha})$ and $\mu$ the M\"obius function.
item.dc:creator: Juan Manzur, Waleed Noor, Gustavo Quintero

item.title: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem in operator algebras
item.description: arXiv:2607.20593v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: The Ulam--Kaplansky problem up to similarity in operator algebras asks whether $A\oplus A\sim B\oplus B$ implies $A\sim B$. We construct block-diagonal compact operators for which this implication fails. For von Neumann algebras with separable predual, we prove that this cancellation property is equivalent to subhomogeneity. Moreover, we obtain a cancellation law for finite ampliations in unital Banach algebras when the commutant of one element is finite dimensional modulo its Jacobson radical.
item.dc:creator: Chunlan Jiang, Minghui Ma, Rui Shi, Yuanhang Zhang

item.title: On Continuous Wavelet Transform of Complex Radon Measures on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$
item.description: arXiv:2610.29293v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This paper investigates a necessary and sufficient condition for a measurable function on $\mathbb{R}^{\times} \times \mathbb{R}^{d}$ to be the continuous wavelet transform of a complex Radon measure on $\mathbb{R}^{d}$ under suitable regularity conditions on the wavelets. We investigate various integrability properties of the wavelet transform of complex Radon measures. We define a new norm on the collection of such functions and show that it is isometrically isomorphic to the Banach algebra of complex Radon measures under convolution. We show a wavelet inversion formula for measures, in a restricted sense. Under additional hypothesis, we provide a reconstruction formula for the measure of closed rectangles in $\mathbb{R}^d$ using wavelet transforms. We have included supporting examples to substantiate these assumptions.
item.dc:creator: Tathagata Banerjee, Vaishakh Jayaprakash

item.title: Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits (revised version)
item.description: arXiv:0905.1311v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: For $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$ and every $n\ge 1$ we construct two $n\times n$ matrices $A$ and $B$ such that the orbit of every vector $p\in\mathbb{K}^n$ with $p_1\ne 0$ under the semigroup generated by $A$ and $B$ is dense in $\mathbb{K}^n$; the remaining vectors lie in an invariant hyperplane, so the set of vectors with dense orbit is exactly the complement of a hyperplane. Thus two generators always suffice for a hypercyclic semigroup of matrices, in contrast with the commutative case, where $n+1$ generators are needed on $\mathbb{C}^n$. We give a transparent reformulation of the hypotheses, a criterion for the density of $\{a^mb^n\}$ that makes them checkable, and explicit examples with complete proofs. As applications we obtain affine pairs on $\mathbb{K}^n$ all of whose orbits are dense, and, for every $n$, a pair of real matrices with an orbit that is somewhere dense but not dense in $\mathbb{R}^n$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Semigroups of matrices with dense orbits, Dyn. Syst. 26 (2011), no. 3, 235--243
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Maximally transitive semigroups of $n\times n$ matrices (revised and extended version)
item.description: arXiv:1201.0192v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Let $\mathbb{K}=\mathbb{R}$ or $\mathbb{C}$. We prove that for every $n\ge 1$ there is a pair of $n\times n$ matrices with entries in $\mathbb{K}$ that generates a dense subsemigroup of the space $M_n(\mathbb{K})$ of all $n\times n$ matrices. Since the powers of a single matrix are never dense, two generators is optimal. Equivalently, there is a $2$-generator semigroup of linear maps whose action on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^n$ is topologically transitive, whereas no semigroup of linear maps acts topologically transitively on $(\mathbb{K}^n)^{n+1}$. In fact, for such a semigroup every orbit closure in $(\mathbb{K}^n)^k$, for every $k\ge1$, is as large as linear algebra allows. Along the way we give a short self-contained proof of the density of explicit $2$-generator subsemigroups of $GL_2^+(\mathbb{R})$ and of $M_2(\mathbb{R})$, based on a simple criterion for closed subsemigroups of $SL_2(\mathbb{R})$.
item.arxiv:journal_reference: M. Javaheri, Maximally transitive semigroups of nxn matrices, J. Math. Anal. Appl. 401 (2013), 743--753
item.dc:creator: Mohammad Javaheri

item.title: Pointwise convergence of noncommutative discrete spherical ergodic averages
item.description: arXiv:2410.06035v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this paper, we establish spherical maximal inequalities associated with commuting trace-preserving automorphisms on von Neumann algebras, extending Magyar-Stein-Wainger's discrete spherical maximal inequalities to the noncommutative setting. On a noncommutative probability space, we further prove that, under a strong ergodicity assumption, the corresponding discrete spherical averages converge bilaterally almost uniformly to $\tau(x)1$ for every $x\in L_p(\mathcal M)$, $\frac{d}{d-2}<p\leq\infty$, when $d\geq5$.
item.dc:creator: Cheng Chen, Guixiang Hong, Wenbo Li

item.title: Langevin Monte-Carlo Provably Learns Depth Two Neural Nets at Any Size and Data
item.description: arXiv:2503.10428v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this note we prove that the Langevin Monte Carlo (LMC) algorithm can minimize the population risk of appropriately regularized depth-2 nets with no restrictions on the size of the net and for any choice of training data --- and we give non-asymptotic convergence rates for it. We achieve this via showing that in q-Renyi divergence, the iterates of LMC converge to the Gibbs distribution of certain Frobenius norm regularized losses for these nets --- in both classification and regression settings. The key technicality of the work is two-fold (a) to keep the amount of regularization needed be independent of the size of the net and (b) to obtain convergence rates that scale with just the Poincare constant of the corresponding Gibbs measure. This work synthesizes several recent observations about isoperimetry conditions under which LMC converges and that two-layer neural loss functions can always be regularized by a constant amount such that they satisfy the Villani conditions, and thus their Gibbs measures satisfy a Poincare inequality.
item.dc:creator: Dibyakanti Kumar, Samyak Jha, Anirbit Mukherjee

item.title: Dynamics in large scale geometry
item.description: arXiv:2604.24452v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We investigate the large scale geometry of certain metric spaces through the lens of dynamics. Our approach establishes a close connection between large scale dynamical phenomena and operator algebras by characterizing various large scale dynamic behaviors in terms of GNS representations of the uniform Roe algebras arising from natural canonical states. Our dynamical systems are given by the Stone-\v{C}ech boundary of metric spaces together with their inverse semigroup of partial translations. This defines a space of orbits and we characterize Hausdorffness and $T_1$-ness of this space by the failure of coarse embeddability of certain metric spaces. Surprisingly, while the orbit space has very weak separation properties, we show that it satisfies a certain ''localized version'' of Urysohn's lemma. We show that the topology of the space of orbits and quasi-orbits are given by the space of irreducible representations of uniform Roe algebras and by the space of their primitive ideals, respectively. As a highlight of the theory developed herein, we provide classes of spaces such that the prime ideals of their uniform Roe algebras are primitive. This is the case for instance of spaces whose orbit space is $T_1$.
item.dc:creator: Bruno de Mendon\c{c}a Braga, Alcides Buss, Ruy Exel

item.title: On the existence of optimizers for nonlinear time-frequency concentration problems: the Born-Jordan distribution
item.description: arXiv:2605.10535v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study the $L^p$ concentration problem for the Born-Jordan distribution in dimension $d>1$, thus extending the one-dimensional analysis in [Stra-Svela-Trapasso, J. Math. Pures Appl. (2026)]. We show that the existence of concentration optimizers depends on the exponent $p$ with a critical threshold at $p_*(d)= \frac{2d}{d-2}$ for $d\geq2$ (with the understanding that $p_*(2)=\infty$). In particular, for subcritical exponents $1\leq p<p_*(d)$ we prove that the supremum is finite and is attained, whereas for supercritical exponents $p>p_*(d)$ we show that the functional is unbounded. We also provide the complete solution in the (significantly more) challenging critical regime in dimension $d=2$. For the critical case in dimension $d=2$ and the supercritical case in dimension $d>2$ we also show that $L^2$ functions whose Born-Jordan distribution does not belong to $L^p$ are generic in the Baire sense. For the critical exponent in dimension $d>2$, for which Wang has recently shown that the supremum is finite, we prove that the functional is not sequentially weakly upper semicontinuous, showing that the still open question of attainment is nontrivial.
item.dc:creator: Federico Stra, Erling A. T. Svela, S. Ivan Trapasso

item.title: The kinetic Kato square root problem
item.description: arXiv:2611.03104v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We solve the kinetic Kato square root problem for the whole-space Kolmogorov operator $$H_A=\partial_t-X\cdot\nabla_Y-\operatorname{div}_X(A\nabla_X)$$ on \(\mathrm L^2\) with Lebesgue measure, where \(A\) is a bounded measurable complex uniformly accretive matrix depending on all variables. We define its realization through a sesquilinear form and identify the square-root domains of the resulting maximal accretive operator and its adjoint with the intrinsic Sobolev space defined by one velocity derivative and half a derivative along the transport flow. The homogeneous norm equivalences depend only on the dimension and the coefficient bounds. The energy also controls a position derivative of order one third. The proof uses second-order resolvents and localized affine testing. A regularized transport symmetrizer gives hidden coercivity, while comparison with a positive Rockland operator supplies intrinsic smoothing. Commutator and dyadic approximation estimates remove the smoothing before a Carleson argument is applied. We also obtain uniform shifted square-root estimates and bounded velocity, transport and position Riesz transforms.
item.dc:creator: Kaj Nystr\"om
